The Babylon set from D.W. Griffith's movie *Intolerance*. It was the most expensive film ever made and a third of the budget was used just for this segment. LA. 1916

Intolerance is a 1916 epic silent film directed by D. W. Griffith. Widely regarded as one of the great masterpieces of the silent era, as well as one of the first art films, the three-and-a-half-hour epic intercuts four parallel storylines, each separated by several centuries.

Intolerance was a colossal undertaking featuring monumental sets, lavish period costumes, and more than 3,000 extras. Actual costs to produce Intolerance are unknown, but best estimates are close to $2.5 million (about $47 million in 2016), an astronomical sum in 1916. A third of the cost went into making the Babylonian segments of the film. The film was by far the most expensive one made up to that time. When it became a flop at the box-office, Griffith, who had mostly self-financed the film, was financially ruined for the rest of his life. As there was no money left to dismantle the set, for a few years it became an actual ruin in the middle of Los Angeles. It was finally torn down in 1919.

AFI's "100 Years...100 Movies" ranked Intolerance at number 49 of 100 films. The film currently holds a 96% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes.

This set was built at the corner of Sunset and Hollywood Boulevards. You may recognize that the look of the Hollywood-Highland Center, which is situated down the street, mimics the look of this set.

Any accutrigger savage, in whatever caliber you want will be a good value hunting gun but with less aftermarket support than a Remington. My first bolt gun was a savage 111 30-06 without the accutrigger but it has been downright deadly accurate for me. The only reason I like the accutrigger is because it just makes a good gun that much better. You can usually find them around $400-500 depending on the model.

Hunting in the desert, you're better off using traps.
But for rifles... my personal favorite would be a Remington 700, chambered for at least 30 cal.
A ruger American in 308 can make that shot reliably. You can get it at Walmart. You will want a nicer scope but that rifle is plent for under 400

Don't know about Walmart's gun selection, but Big5 has some good enough bolt guns that would easily handle such a task. Remmington 700 (or other 7-series, like 770, Model 7, 783 which is the cheapest, I think) comes to mind, also they have some Savages that would work. You could even pull it off with a .308 Ruger Gunsite Scout if you're a good shot, not too cheap though. They also have carbine length ARs, which are easy enough to maintain in the field, but probably not going to have as good of accuracy at that range as a bolt action, and will usually cost more. Their reliability will also suffer more over time in the sandy desert than a simple bolt gun. If I had to use a rifle off the shelf, with the only mod being an optic, I'd probably lean towards the Remington.

Edit: forgot about Ruger American, also a fine choice.
